sections.content:
Population change in Reading in 2032

The population in Reading is projected to increase from 175,742 people in 2022 to 181,884 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 28,788 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Reading
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Reading, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 6,849, with 19,203 births and 12,355 deaths in Reading between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Reading by 3.9%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 28,225, with 144,747 people moving to the area and 172,972 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Reading by 16.1%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,271, with 5,981 people moving to the area and 7,252 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Reading by 0.7%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 28,788, with 55,000 people moving to the area and 26,212 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Reading by 16.4%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Reading in 2032

The median age in Reading is projected to rise from 35 years in 2022 to 36 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 13% of the population in Reading are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 11% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Reading between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Reading is projected to stay the same, at around 71%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 165 to 172 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Reading?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Reading between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
